Aisha Kapoor: ok draft should include: what happened, who was impacted, mitigation we applied, customer-facing remediation steps we recommend, and next steps/compensatory credits if any. be concise.
Olivia Chen: draft 1 below — please edit inline. aim for email + short status page blurb.

incidents-bot: Incident 2026-03-19-EBS: embeddings service high tail latency — created by Ben Thompson at 2026-03-19T03:12:00Z. Severity: Sev2.
Olivia Chen: DRAFT EMAIL:

Hi <customer>,

We’re reaching out about an interruption to Redwood Embeddings ingestion and query latency on 2026-03-19 between 03:01–03:38 UTC that impacted a subset of tenants, including your account.

What happened:
- A memory leak in the embeddings worker process caused OOM restarts on 3 nodes handling embedding queries.
- This resulted in increased tail latency and some request errors for ~37 minutes.
- No customer data was accessed or exfiltrated; requests that errored can be retried safely.

What we did to mitigate:
- Automatically rebalanced traffic away from affected nodes at 03:12 UTC.
- Rolled a targeted hotfix to close the memory leak at 03:29 UTC.
- Manually drained and restarted the 3 nodes; full service restored at 03:38 UTC.

Impact to you:
- Potential increased latency or 5xx errors for embedding requests during the window.
- Any requests that failed should be retried; we can help replay if needed.

Next steps we are taking:
- Deploying an improved memory-sanitization build to all clusters by 2026-03-20.
- Adding proactive OOM alerting and automatic routing cutover to avoid client impact.
- Running a sweep to identify any long-running jobs that may have contributed.

If you’d like, we can set up a 30-minute call to walk through specifics for your workloads and help replay any failed requests.

We apologize for the disruption and are prioritizing measures to prevent recurrence.

— Olivia (Customer Success) on behalf of the Redwood Reliability team
